In the six files, the only matches left are production code: xtask/src/main.rs:809 (fn set_executable, used at 415/490/550) and crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:445/453/478 (outside the tests module). criteria.criterion: The helper source in crates/athena-testkit/src/lib.rs spawns sh with the script bytes on stdin running cat to a temp file, chmod 755, then mv to the final path, waits for it, and never opens the script for writing in the test process.
criteria.evidence: lib.rs:32 has WRITE_SCRIPT = `cat > "$1" && chmod 755 -- "$1" && mv -- "$1" "$2"`. Lines 50-64 spawn `sh -c` with the temp path (same directory, unique per pid and counter) and the final path as positional arguments. The code writes the contents to a piped stdin, drops the pipe, and calls wait_with_output. A non-zero exit becomes an error that carries stderr. The test process opens no file handle on the path.

findings.summary: Soundness: the scan only matches the names set_permissions, from_mode and set_mode, so it misses the regression that failed the previous job. A test that writes a stand-in in-process and then calls a production wrapper such as xtask's `set_executable`, or runs the external `chmod`, passes the scan.
findings.evidence: Scanner::record keeps only names in FLAGGED. Reading the code: `std::fs::write(&fake, ..); set_executable(&fake);` in xtask's #[cfg(test)] module (xtask/src/main.rs:807 is reachable through `use super::*`) would record `set_executable`, which is not flagged, and the body at :809 counts as production code. That is the exact pattern from job 20261106-065752-jexx (its verification.json:158). `std::fs::write` followed by `Command::new("chmod")` is not flagged either, yet the race comes from the in-process write. The reading wanted the scan to fail on 'any in-process executable write in test code'. Simpler fix: first collect every workspace function whose body calls a flagged name (here xtask set_executable, pin::set_writable, toolconfig::set_executable, snapshot::set_mode) and flag test-code calls to those too. Add a planted-violation unit test for `set_executable(&fake)`, and optionally flag string literals `chmod` in Command args in test code.

summary: The retry fixes all four findings from job 20261106-065752-jexx. The xtask gitleaks test now calls athena_testkit::write_executable. The CHANGELOG entry matches the diff. docs/architecture.md gains only the athena-testkit row. The ETXTBSY counts now show in a normal test run: I ran `cargo test --locked -p athena-testkit` and got "ETXTBSY runs with write_executable: 0 of 480" and "...in-process write: 3 of 480". The helper is correct: it pipes the script into `sh -c 'cat > tmp && chmod 755 tmp && mv tmp final'` and waits, so the test process never opens the file for writing. All six test sites are converted, and the retry loop in reading.rs is gone. D157 and its link (line 4318) are in place, and the fmt, clippy and test records all passed. Every acceptance criterion is met. The verdict is still fail, because of one major soundness gap in the scan test, the mechanism meant to keep tests on the helper. It flags only three API names (set_permissions, from_mode, set_mode). A test that writes a script and then calls a wrapper, such as xtask's own `set_executable` (xtask/src/main.rs:807, reachable from the tests through `use super::*`), passes the scan. That is exactly the site that failed the previous job. So does a test that runs `std::fs::write` and then calls the external `chmod`. The scan would let the same regression back in.
